Folded arXiv:2609.02992 (Tempting the Agent: The Economics of Reputation without Persistent Identity; Gatta, Naviglio, Tarantelli; 2026-09-02). A dynamic model: reputation disciplines an agent only when abandoning an identity is costly. The agent deviates (milk reputation, then reset to a penalised fresh identity) when extracted value minus reset cost >= 0. Prop 4.4: a full reset disciplines better than a degraded identity - IF reset is costly. Prop 4.8: HIGH reputation can INCREASE temptation (extractable value grows faster than the preservation benefit). Corollary 5.3: explicit honesty thresholds in kappa_R (reset cost), rho (decay), staking. Fixes: bind identity to a verifiable principal, detection-coupled slashing, calibrate decay. LANDS ON tools/reputation.py: the substrate makes reset FREE (unauthenticated agent field => kappa_R ~ 0), so it sits on the wrong side of every threshold; the UCB exploration bonus that keeps reputation non-calcifying ALSO subsidises a whitewashing reset (unpriced tension); Prop 4.8 = the emergent 'personal assistant' role is the high-value target with no slash a reset can't erase. +1 node, +7 edges.
